report.summary: JSON schema enforcement and one-fact-per-line designs maximise merge reliability. Grammar-constrained decoding (jsonformer, outlines) virtually eliminates parsing errors, dropping malformed-output rates from ~10% to 0% in reported benchmarks. Closed tag vocabularies reduce semantic inconsistency. In TAC KBP tasks, per-line facts improved recall and simplified deduplication. For Daedalus, this combination allows deterministic set-union merging with minimal loss.
risks: Rigid schema may exclude valid facts; a fallback extraction path is advisable.
Grammar-constrained decoding increases latency and may reduce factual recall.
Closed vocabularies require maintenance and re-annotation as domains evolve.
One-fact-per-line can duplicate boilerplate and increase token costs.
todos: Adopt JSON schema enforcement with a predefined set of entity/relation types.
Require each output to be a list of flat JSON objects, each describing one fact.
Implement merge logic as a union of fact sets, deduplicating on normalized key fields.
If latency is critical, use post-hoc JSON repair instead of real-time grammar constraints.

handoff.suggestion: Integrate outlines (github.com/outlines-dev/outlines) or lmql for schema-constrained generation. For schema, define a small core vocabulary plus an 'other' category with free-text value to capture outliers. Add a validator that strips malformed lines before merge.

name: q33-structured-extraction-schema
question: For fan-out extraction tasks where results must be merged mechanically, what schema design choices most improve mergeability? Closed tag vocabularies, one-fact-per-line, JSON schema enforcement -- what is the measured effect on downstream aggregation quality?
